substantive_delta: One uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm for the entire immutable unit-capacity undirected AON input class achieves C log(k+2) exp(C sqrt(log log(k+4))) approximation with exact congestion one, distinct original admissions, always feasible output and probability at least 3/4, improving the primary-source O(log^2 k) baseline.
why_nonroutine: The result does not merely substitute an improved bound into adaptive throughput decomposition. A fixed feasible uniform path family permits a cut-loss charge while protected original occurrence cuts convert unit copy selection to distinct original admission; the uniform scale cancels in the one-shot decomposition/rounding yield. The exact small-k branch removes the remaining n-versus-k obstruction. Uniformization, clustering and flow decomposition are credited as known. Their admission-preserving interface yields a new full-target algorithm rather than a restricted or subsidiary corollary.
significance: It reduces nearly one logarithmic exponent for a standard nonlinear admission/routing model on all undirected unit-capacity graphs without congestion augmentation, resolving the exact recent BJS conjecture and the stated older O(log^2 k) benchmark. This is substantive mathematical value; the separate venue assessment is conservative about technical depth and broader consequences.
